identity.name: CNM × Stack to Nearby Chests Compatibility
aliases: Clutter No More × Stack to Nearby Chests Compatibility
legacy_names: Clutter No More × Stack to Nearby Chests Compatibility

goals: Preserve the historical standalone design contract for treating Clutter No More geometry variants with the same exact canonical source material as one Stack to Nearby Chests destination family.
Preserve the frozen retirement decision and exact accepted successor direction without reviving, redesigning, or claiming the separate Quick Stack Nearby compatibility integration.
Keep the parked identity distinct from Block Geometry Extensions, Matcha × Stack to Nearby Chests, and Quick Stack Nearby compatibility.
scope: The unimplemented standalone C1 design used symmetric destination-family admission: any full block or recognized slab, stair, wall, vertical slab, or step could establish a destination when Clutter No More resolved both items to the same exact source material; actual Stack to Nearby Chests insertion would otherwise remain unchanged and different geometry would remain separate stacks.

The frozen accepted successor is separately owned Quick Stack Nearby compatibility: exact Clutter No More ShapeMap admission feeds Quick Stack Nearby's normal component-aware merge path, so the existing destination geometry wins. This parked UUID owns no successor code, artifact, or acceptance result.
Exact source variants remain distinct, including log and wood, stripped and unstripped, waxed and unwaxed, oxidation states, coral states, terracotta treatments, and colors.
Canonical family identity comes from the selected Clutter No More/provider architecture and never from registry-name suffixes or a second project-owned material database.

exclusions: Reactivating, redesigning, or implementing the retired standalone adapter during this migration.

Claiming Block Geometry Extensions, Nibaru, Clutter No More, Stack to Nearby Chests, Matcha × Stack to Nearby Chests, or Quick Stack Nearby compatibility identity, source, artifacts, or runtime evidence as this project.
Registry-name parsing, fuzzy material equivalence, source-variant collapse, item conversion, general dump-all behavior, reserved-slot behavior, or nested-container routing.
Importing legacy status READMEs, BUILD_PROVENANCE files, historical matrices, global databases, deployment history, snapshots, or other superseded administration.
Runtime deployment, Minecraft launch, Test Slot A/B changes, accepted-baseline changes, dedicated Workbench access, or protected gameplay-instance access during this migration.
Any modification to originals or to paths outside projects/cnm-stack-to-nearby-chests-compat.
